complexity_ledger.narrative: EP-02 adds a versioned stable seed protocol, bounded campaign iteration, exact single-point replay, structured lifecycle diagnostics, project-owned provider scaffolds, and small context-stack/temporary-root helpers. Provider configuration and lazy binding are prepared across the corpus before any application hook; each runtime point then gets isolated singleton batch hooks, adapter/shared caches, provider resources, and opaque work paths. Provider allocation and cleanup sit outside passive application observation, while adapter setup/run/assertion/teardown remains within both provider and observation scopes. This prevents harness filesystem churn from becoming a false effect without hiding application calls through injected bindings or installed patches. Review corrections, exact validation, explicit limits, and the zero-model-delta rationale are recorded in results/validation-summary.md, results/review-correction.txt, and results/zero-model-delta.md.

summary: Add deterministic provider campaigns, exact replay, project-owned helper scaffolds, and effect-safe lifecycle isolation with zero host-model delta.

assertions: Same seed, cases, and providers produce the same iteration order, derived seeds, responses, and failure; the emitted replay command reproduces the failing case/iteration.
A custom project provider can be written and selected without changing framework code; generated scaffolding exposes the full required contract without hidden imports.
Library helpers cover one explicit-injection filesystem shape and one generic self-installed patch/context-manager shape, with cleanup on success and every failure phase.
Docs explain the semantic boundary between TLA+ cases and provider-owned concrete responses/state, including when a new TLA+ case or independent oracle is required.
Docs do not claim universal interception, exhaustive fuzzing, shrinking, or correctness stronger than the provider and case oracle provide.
SKILL.md edits are validated from this branch; no global skill-manager sync occurs before the epic reaches the default branch.
Zero host TLA+ model delta unless implementation adds observable CLI state; current == desired and TLC/spec-unit evidence records the decision.

ticket.objective: Make EP-01 usable by a project author without expanding it into a framework-owned simulator. Add a small provider kit: an explicit temporary-root filesystem helper and a generic context-manager/patch provider factory, plus generated provider stubs. Add bounded CLI fuzz iteration (`--fuzz-runs N --seed S`) with a stable derived seed for each case, iteration, and port, deterministic ordering, and copy-paste replay diagnostics on every failure. The provider receives the immutable generated case plus run metadata and owns concrete response generation, state, and assertions. It may fuzz concrete representatives inside the modeled semantic outcome; it must not rewrite the case's expected output/after state. Document how users implement filesystem, HTTP, Kafka, SMTP, or domain-specific providers, and be explicit that fuzzing depth is bounded by provider capability. Do not add a central Hypothesis campaign, exhaustive cross-product, shrinking claim, real Kafka/SMTP libraries, or generated per-call response scripts in this ticket.
ticket.title: Provider authoring kit and deterministic fuzz/replay loop
